title: ApplyBoard was the worst-performing Canadian startup in Fidelity’s portfolio in 2026
ai_summary: Fidelity's stake in ApplyBoard, a Canadian student-education platform, fell about two-thirds in 2026, from $113 million to $5.4 million. The writedown is likely dragging down Fidelity's overall Canadian venture returns, according to a consultant. ApplyBoard's valuation had peaked at $4 billion in 2021 before policy changes.

title: Ex-ApplyBoard CEO now competing with his former company – led by his brother – as Passage lands testing deal
ai_summary: Passage Inc., founded by former ApplyBoard CEO Martin Basiri, has secured an exclusive strategic partnership with Educational Testing Service (ETS) to integrate its AI agents into TOEFL and GRE testing processes. This development positions Passage as a direct competitor to ApplyBoard, which is led by Martin's brother Meti and continues to streamline international student applications using similar AI technologies. The move occurs amidst broader industry challenges, including reduced immigration approvals and declining revenues for key players like ApplyBoard.

title: Lume Test Collaborates with ApplyBoard to Offer Discounted English Test Vouchers
ai_summary: Lume Test has announced a collaboration with ApplyBoard to become an authorized partner, enabling students in selected countries to purchase discounted English proficiency test vouchers for PTE Academic, PTE Core, and the Duolingo English Test through the Lume Test platform. The partnership aims to make English proficiency testing more affordable and accessible by combining exam preparation tools with voucher purchasing in one integrated experience. Lume Test stated this collaboration represents a development as it expands support available to learners worldwide pursuing international education, migration, and career goals.

title: Canada sharpens focus on study permit finances; proof of funds under scanner - The Economic Times
ai_summary: Canada's Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC) has updated guidance for study permit applications, directing officers to scrutinize not just the amount but also the source, stability, and credibility of applicants' funds more broadly than before. An ApplyBoard analysis of 1,370 refusal letters found inadequate proof of finances was the leading rejection reason at 47%, while approval rates for major source countries including India (13 percentage points) and Nigeria (8 percentage points) improved during the first four months of 2026 despite the stricter requirements. Canadian educational institutions are being urged to shift from volume-based recruitment to focusing on applicants better prepared to meet the stricter financial documentation standards.

title: Canadian immigration officials increase their scrutiny of study permit applicants’ financial documentation
ai_summary: Canadian immigration officials are increasing scrutiny of study permit applicants' financial documentation, leading to a 43% drop in new applications but a 9 percentage point increase in the approval rate to 35% between January and April 2026. IRCC updated its guidance on July 24, 2026, directing officers to thoroughly investigate funding sources and request supplementary financial evidence for all cases rather than just high-risk environments. Analysis by BorderPass and ApplyBoard indicates that unclear proof of funds remains the primary reason for refusal, prompting recommendations for stricter documentation standards like six months of bank statements and sponsor job letters.
